solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parton shock! Kinky hole in bra cut by director

indicators.note: cut by means the director's letter slices into the rearranged letters
kinky means twisted, so the letters of the three words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid shriek about a racy piece of lingerie being snipped by a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' scrambles HOLE IN BRA to BLONEHAIR, and 'cut by' puts D inside it. Dolly Parton, the country singer, is famous for her shock of platinum hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick mass of hair, and Dolly Parton's trademark is a pale golden one.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps enjoying new joke in the 26

indicators.note: enjoying means having or holding, so the toilet holds the other pieces

parts.note: the Ladies is a public toilet, a loo
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Women chuckling at a fresh joke in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 is PAST (26-across), so the definition reads 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened in the past happened a great while back, in former times.

clue.text: Coward welcomes White Christmas

indicators.note: welcomes means the playwright's name takes the letter in

parts.note: Noel Coward was the English playwright and songwriter

explanation.surface: A playwright greets the famous Bing Crosby song about a snowy festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowel is an old spelling of the carol word for the Christmas festival.

clue.text: 8's last word, the very one top pair ignored

indicators.note: in a down light the top pair are the first two letters of the phrase, left off so the rest is read on

explanation.surface: Someone's final statement is identified as the exact one, with the leading two set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is TINY TIM, whose closing line in the story is 'God bless us, every one!'
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny Tim ends the Dickens tale with the blessing on all and sundry, so this phrase is literally his final utterance.

clue.text: Book alarms nearly 16 so terribly

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the pooled letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nearly means without the final letter

parts.note: 16 is the clerk Cratchit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel frightens a nearly complete character very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims CRATCHIT to CRATCHI; 'terribly' shuffles ALARMS + CRATCHI + SO into the Dickens title.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's festive novella is a book, published in 1843 about Scrooge's ghostly night.

clue.text: First of rickety old trucks' regular journeys

indicators.note: First of signals only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: utes are small pickup trucks, an Australian term

explanation.surface: Battered old lorries make the same trips again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Routes are the set courses taken repeatedly by buses, deliveries and travellers.

clue.text: Sherpa might yell: "It's over behind you!"

indicators.note: behind means the reversed piece comes after the other one

parts.note: ye is an old word for you

indicators.note: over means turned around, read the other way

parts.note: the word it, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: A mountain guide shouts a pantomime warning that something is lurking at your back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IT to TI, placed 'behind' YE. The surface echoes the pantomime cry 'It's behind you!'
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalaya is what a mountain guide might shout about on seeing it.

clue.text: Last visitor in 5 still in my opinion holds firm

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'still to arrive'

indicators.note: holds means the phrase surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to me means in my opinion
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone's view remains steady and unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is A CHRISTMAS CAROL, whose final spirit is the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.
explanation.definitionFit: The third and last ghost to call on Scrooge is the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.

clue.text: Invalid 16 plea may be rendered impatiently

indicators.note: rendered means turned into, so the letters of the clue word plus the plea rearrange to impatiently

explanation.surface: A request might be delivered with irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus PLEA rearrange to make IMPATIENTLY. 16 is CRATCHIT; his crippled son is the invalid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Cratchit's sickly youngest son, walking with a crutch, is the invalid of the Cratchit family.

clue.text: Jon's last bit of news, 18

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: 18 is PRESENT, which means now

explanation.surface: A newsreader delivers the closing item of the bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: Jon Snow was a long-serving British television newsreader; 's here is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jon Snow is the full name of the Channel 4 News presenter, so the forename defines his surname.

clue.text: Like old endless election campaign one enters?

definitions.text: Like old endless election campaign one enters?

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: enters means the letter goes into the trimmed word
endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: the hustings are the campaign of speeches before an election
A means one

explanation.surface: Describing a seemingly never-ending political race a candidate joins.
explanation.walkthrough: The election campaign is the hustings, the round of speeches; trimmed and with one inside, it follows the word for old. The question mark marks the whole clue as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A long drawn-out campaign is tiring and draining, wearing out everyone who takes part.

clue.text: First visitor in 5 might introduce regular relief

indicators.note: introduce means the selected letters are put inside the verb

parts.note: may means might

indicators.note: regular picks every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something that could bring routine comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular' takes R, L, E from relief, and they go inside MAY. Bob Marley the singer misdirects too.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Marley's ghost is the first apparition to call on Scrooge in the Dickens story.

clue.text: They're equipped with powerful bows and live over in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the other letters
nova is Latin for new, so the following word is made new, rearranged
over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: be means live, exist

explanation.surface: Canadian craft with strong prows are based in the Maritimes province.
explanation.walkthrough: Nova Scotia is a Canadian province; 'Nova' is Latin for new, here the anagram signal, and 'over' turns live round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels for frozen waters have reinforced prows that can cut through the floes.

clue.text: United but perhaps without No 1 back

indicators.note: without means the letters are taken away

parts.note: but is an example of a conjunction

indicators.note: back means read in reverse

parts.note: No is short for number, written NO, and 1 is I

explanation.surface: Joined together, though possibly missing the top person returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO I into ION, removed from CONJUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjunct is a formal adjective meaning joined or combined together.

clue.text: 22 upset after gag about Charles's top hat at Ascot

indicators.note: after means the turned word follows
about means the jest goes around the initial

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the next word, in a down light
upset means turned upside down, in a down light read upwards

parts.note: 22 is METEORIC, meaning very fast, and pacy means fast

explanation.surface: A fast-paced jest about a royal headwear at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is METEORIC, very fast. Ascot is a famous English racecourse where jockeys wear peaked silk headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders at Ascot races wear a peaked silk headgear of this kind.

clue.text: Frank marking degrees of resistance

definitions.meaning: a frank is a postal stamp mark, and On Her Majesty's Service was printed on official mail

explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for On Her Majesty's Service franked official post, and the unit of resistance is named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Lord's cry about radical clerk in 5

indicators.note: about means the shout goes around the letter

parts.note: at Lord's cricket ground a fielder may shout 'catch it'
R is the abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A peer exclaims about an extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, so the cry is a fielder's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's underpaid clerk in the Dickens tale.

clue.text: French grocer's exporting water on a vast scale

indicators.note: exporting means sending out, so those letters leave

parts.note: an epicerie is a French grocer's shop
Lake Erie is a body of water

explanation.surface: A shop in France ships out its bottled drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand, heroic and huge in size or scope.

clue.text: Third visitor in 5's tense

definitions.meaning: the Ghost of Christmas ... is the third spirit to call, counting Marley
a grammatical tense, as opposed to past or future

explanation.definitionFit: The Ghost of Christmas Present visits Scrooge, and it is also the grammatical tense for now.

clue.text: Dopes nuts with 1, but not leader

indicators.note: but not leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: 1 is BLONDE HAIR, and its second word supplies the piece
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Idiots are crazy alongside the blonde, though not the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: From 1's second word drop the leader to leave AIR. The dumb-blonde joke links to 1-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopes and airheads are both slang for silly, empty-headed people.

clue.text: Estate's seedsmen pulling the first crackers

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the remaining letters go wild
pulling means removing, the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Gardeners on a country property are going mad having lost their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling the first' takes S from seedsmen, then 'crackers' rearranges EEDSMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor house, a landed property.

clue.text: Don's one-time advantage

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, a prof; 's is a link
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A university lecturer's former benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or benefit, an edge one gains from something.

clue.text: What Ernie did initially, earning love very fast

indicators.note: earning means gaining, so the piece takes in the letter

parts.note: Ernie Wise first met Eric Morecambe, the comedy duo
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A comic's early earnings rise at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a famous British comedy double act; Ernie MET ERIC at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteoric means rapid and dazzling, like a meteor streaking across the sky.

clue.text: Add big spaces for family emblems

parts.note: tot up means add
an em is a wide printing space

explanation.surface: Instructions to insert large gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Totems are objects or animals serving as symbols of a clan or kin group.

clue.text: He records spill

definitions.meaning: a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire

explanation.definitionFit: A taper is both a thin candle or spill for lighting and someone making recordings on tape.

clue.text: From now on nothing stops the French working

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the letter goes inside
working means in operation, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: From today zero halts French labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles THE FRENCH, and 'stops' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth is a formal adverb meaning from this time onward.

clue.text: Second visitor in 5 went by, say

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: passed means went by

explanation.surface: Someone strolled by.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ghost of Christmas Past is the second spirit to visit Scrooge, after Marley.

clue.text: Block what Scrooge had withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so read in reverse

parts.note: Scrooge had pots of money

explanation.surface: Barring what the miser took out from the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to block or obstruct something.

clue.text: Gobble treat?

parts.note: gobbling is how a turkey talks, and to treat is to negotiate frankly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to discuss business frankly, while gobble is literally what a turkey says.
